verdict: SHIP, narrowly scoped - like Q010, not like Q014. All four pre-registered SHIP conjuncts were met and independently reproduced at a third n value: a MethodInfo for a function defined only inside a live FsiEvaluationSession (plugin text read at runtime, never compiled by the host) was handed back across the FSI/host boundary, confirmed to genuinely originate from FSI's dynamic assembly (not the host's), and Expr.TryGetReflectedDefinition returned the identical quotation shape Q014 got at host-compile-time - closing Q014's specific 'no FSI ran / both pieces were compile-time literals' gap. But the review found FSI performs none of the actual staging: it compiles the plugin and hands back a MethodInfo via a quotation-destructure one-liner that never executes power; 100% of the partial evaluation is host-compiled code byte-identical to Q014. The origin is dynamic-body/static-interface only - the host still hardcodes the plugin's name, arity, and types, and unroll is still hand-matched to power's exact shape. Composition with Myriad's real architecture (ALC-isolated plugin loading, config from parsed attributed source) remains untested. See 03-review.md for the full adversarial review and four named follow-ups.
